text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Suspected links between organised crime and Environment Minister Ferenc Baja, chairman of the Socialist Party board, prompted the Intelligence Office to collecte data on four Socialist MPs, reports Vilaggazdasag. The four politicians in question are Baja, Speaker of Parliament Zoltan Gal, MP and MOL executive Laszlo Pal and MP Tibor Bajor. Nepszabadsag writes that data was also gathered on Socialist MP Gabor Kiss and independent MP Peter Tolgyessy.

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn said in Parliament yesterday that various political forces, including parliamentary parties, have of late been making efforts to heighten tensions in various areas of society. Meanwhile Gabor Szalay, on behalf of the Free Democrats called on the Smallholders to urge deputy speaker Agnes Maczo to resign due to political anti-Semitism.

- Gyorgy Zsikla, vice president of the militant Agricultural Producers' Advocacy Organisation said that they will continue the demonstrations during the agricultural round table conference of April 25. Meanwhile the National Federation of Hungarian Farmers' Societies released a statement saying the problems should be resolved in Parliament rather than on roads.
- Companies exporting products to the EU containing parts imported from non-EU countries may no longer request an import duty refund, according to a customs bill expected to take effect July 1.

- Slovak representatives yesterday argued before the International Court of Justice that the dispute over the Gabcikovo-Nagymaros hydropower plant is not an environmental protection matter, as claimed by Hungary, but a simple dispute over a treaty.
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs said a special EU meeting on the results of the Maastricht treaty review conference will be held on June 27 for East European countries seeking membership.
- The Defence Ministry is seeking parliamentary approval to allow up to 300 NATO planes to fly over Hungarian airspace and to refuel at Hungarian airports.
- The economic boom begun in the second half of last year continued in January, the Central Statistical Office reports, based on its analysis of first month figures.
- The National Bank of Hungary raised the annual interest rate on six-month fixed deposits by banks to 21 percent.
- Transport Minister Karoly Lotz yesterday sacked Sandor Kis Kalnoki as president of the Hungarian Railway and terminated the position.
- The International Committee of the Red Cross will set up a regional office in Budapest.
NEPSZABADSAG
- The British government will support the expansion and overhaul of the Peto Institute to the tune of 2 million under a pact to be signed today.
- Papal Nuncio Angelo Acerbi was Monday honoured by President Arpad Goncz.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- The export price of domestic corn fell by DM20 per ton over the last month.
- The Dutch ING Bank is among several international financial institutions interested in bidding on K&H Bank.
- The chemical manufacturer BorsodChem has founded a trading company in Poland.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The Hungarian Telecommunications company Matav is preparing a HUF 6-8 billion bond issue for early April.
